options: A layer of space around the nucleus where electrons orbit
The dense core of the atom
A type of bond between atoms
The outer skin of a molecule
questions.explanation: An electron shell is a layer of space around the nucleus at a fixed distance, where electrons orbit.
questions.misconception: The dense core is the nucleus and bonds are connections between atoms — the shell is specifically the orbital layer around the nucleus where electrons live.

questions.prompt: How many electrons can the first (innermost) shell hold?
questions.explanation: The first shell, closest to the nucleus, holds at most 2 electrons. The second holds up to 8, and later shells can hold more.
questions.misconception: The 8-electron capacity belongs to the second shell — the innermost shell is smaller and caps out at just 2.

questions.prompt: In what order do electrons fill the shells?
options: Inner shells first, then outer shells
questions.explanation: Electrons fill the inner shells first, then the outer ones — the atom builds its layers from the inside out.
questions.misconception: Electrons never jump to the outer shells while inner shells are empty — the filling order is strictly inner-first.

questions.prompt: Which shell decides how an atom bonds?
questions.explanation: The outermost shell's electrons — the valence electrons — are the ones shared, lost, or gained when atoms bond.
questions.misconception: The inner shells are buried and do not interact with other atoms — chemistry happens entirely at the outermost shell.
